title: LinkedIn posts no longer cut short

blocks.text: A post holding brackets, parentheses, an @ or a # no longer stops short on LinkedIn, and its hashtags stay live. A post that went out on one account but failed for good on another now reads as published, with the failed account still shown in its queue. A long post is never cut through the middle of an emoji.

On a post with pictures, Attach the clean picture takes the AI marks out of the picture files: the Content Credentials LinkedIn shows as a CR badge, and the tags the image generator writes. Each marked picture is redrawn without them, saved to the Assets Library and put on the post as a new picture version. The picture looks the same, and the original stays in the versions.

title: Image anonymizer reads from the Assets Library

blocks.text: Next to the drop box, From the Assets Library opens the team's pictures, 15 a page, newest first, with a search by name or tag and filters. The picture is cleaned as it is stored, and the library copy is never changed.

Create named campaigns to group assets from your library, including texts, pictures, videos and documents. Add assets from the campaign page or directly from the library, and give teammates brief instructions. Campaigns also appear in your team rights so you can control who can view or edit them.

A new Agents module: the Social publishing watcher re-reads your publishing on every network on a schedule and tells you what changed, and you can build agents of your own over your posts, campaigns and library. Run one now or on a schedule, and read its findings and runs.
Social posts now keep every set of pictures they carried as versions, so you can pick v1, v2 and more. Use a past version to restore it and the files remain in your Assets Library.
Open a post's image in the Image editor or its video in the Video editor straight from the post. Editing updates are saved back to your library and the post can be updated to use the edited file.

title: Saved skills and materials with posts

blocks.text: When you create Instagram, TikTok or YouTube posts, the Skills and material you pick are now saved with the post. Those choices are used when the caption is written so your tone and brief stay consistent.

title: Quick, Balanced and Best model picks

blocks.text: Text model pickers now offer Quick, Balanced and Best choices with the cost per run shown and a link to model benchmarks in Settings. Administrators can set the three defaults for the team.
Image, video and caption engine pickers now open defaulted to the least expensive available engine so you see cost-efficient options first.

Screens no longer show brand controls, which hubStudio never used: the Brand voice switch, Check voice and the Brand column of the Assets Library are gone. English screens say team again instead of organization.
Accounts that have not been used for two months receive a warning email and will be deactivated after a further month unless the person signs in. Nothing is deleted by this process.
Accepted file types for YouTube uploads now match YouTube's current list, so unsupported formats are no longer offered during upload.

title: Transparent backgrounds only where they work

blocks.text: ChatGPT Image 2 no longer offers a transparent background, which it cannot make, so a render no longer fails on it. The ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines still cut the subject out.
Campaign summary cards now count documents the same way the campaign page does, so asset counts are accurate at a glance.

The LinkedIn connection steps now say to keep your profile and the company pages you post for, and to remove the ones you do not. They no longer tell you to leave company pages to the team: social accounts are personal.

Buttons that cannot be used now appear visually disabled: they are greyed out, show a no entry cursor and do not change on hover in both light and dark modes. Busy buttons still show their spinner and pulse so you know an action is in progress.

title: Set each member's modules and rights

blocks.text: On the Team page, Details opens a member's own page, where an admin switches their modules on or off and sets their rights, then Back to the team returns to the list. Rights now cover Assets, the Image editor, the Video editor, Shorts autopilot and Validation, and a module someone may not view leaves their menu. New rights follow the role until an admin changes them.

title: YouTube videos and a channel kit

blocks.text: hubStudio now has a YouTube module. Render the video with AI, pick it from the Assets Library or upload it, and AI writes its title and description to YouTube's rules: a title of up to 100 characters and a description of up to 5,000, both checked and fixed. Publish interactively downloads the video and opens the YouTube Studio upload window with the title ready to paste, then Copy the description carries the rest, and you publish it there yourself. The Channel tab prepares your team's channel: its name, handle, description, keywords, links, a banner and a profile picture sized for YouTube, then walks you through opening it on YouTube.

title: Connecting a social account shows what you allow

blocks.text: When you connect TikTok, its permission page now always appears, even for an account you connected before. Instagram asks you to sign in and confirm every time, so you can pick another professional account. Connecting Facebook again offers the pages and permissions you left out the last time.

Translations for French and Chinese were polished across the app, including the report a bug page, validation and approval queues, image editor badges and social reporting dates. Translated text no longer overwrites your saved content, so task titles, feed items and reports stay exactly as you wrote them. Layouts and typography were adjusted so longer French labels fit, Chinese uses a clean sans fallback, numbers and units follow French notation, and French mail recipients now show "À".

hubStudio now speaks English, French and Chinese, from the menu to every screen. Pick your language in the menu under your picture or in User Settings, and the help center is there in the three languages too.
A new Languages card on the Team page lets admins pick the interface languages the team can switch to. English is always on; what the team writes and makes keeps its own language.

In French, amounts, file sizes and video lengths now read the French way, with a space between thousands and a decimal comma (20 000, 2,5), in the studios, the editors, Shorts autopilot and the balance pages.

title: One email for new AI models

blocks.text: When new AI models arrive, you now get one email that lists them all instead of one email per model. The subject names the model when there is one and counts them when there are several, and the models added during a day go out together the next morning.
When a button or a form takes you to another page, the loading overlay now appears straight away instead of after a short pause, so the screen never looks frozen while the next page opens.

Each tool now has its own page and menu entry, including Image editor, Image anonymizer, Video editor and Shorts autopilot. Tool pages show the tool name in the header and no longer list other tools, and the Assets Library is now a single entry.

The Image anonymizer was moved out of the Assets Library into its own standalone tool you can enable or disable per person. Access to it is tied to the Image permission so team admins can control who sees the tool.
Page header bands are more compact and the left menu is denser, with menu groups folded by default so you can scan content faster.
The link in the welcome email of a person added to a team now works for 5 days instead of 24 hours, and only once.

title: Shorts autopilot, the editors in the menu, and a Social panel in the Video editor

blocks.text: Shorts autopilot joins the menu: give it a long video, such as an interview, a talk or a podcast, and it cuts its best moments into vertical 9:16 shorts for YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels by itself. It listens to every word (free in your browser, or faster with a paid option whose price shows before you start), keeps the moments that open on a hook and tell one complete idea, frames each one around the person speaking, and adds captions word by word and a hook line over the first seconds. Each short is saved in the Assets Library next to the original, with a score, a title and a caption for each network to copy, and opens in the Video editor for a last touch. The run shows in Activity. It also starts from Make shorts in a video's Actions menu in the Assets Library. The Image editor and the Video editor now have their own entries in the menu too, and the Assets Library's Tools open on the Image anonymizer. The Video editor gains a Social panel: pick Instagram, TikTok or Facebook and a placement (a reel, a story, a feed post), crop every clip or fit it whole over a blurred copy, see in red what the network's buttons and caption cover, with a Zones switch to show or hide them, preview the cover on the profile grid, and read the checks, each with a button to fix what it found. The pencil on the clip of an Instagram, TikTok or Facebook post opens the editor on that panel, set to the network.

title: Video editor for Reels and TikToks, and a Social panel in the Image editor

blocks.text: The Assets Library's Tools gain a Video editor, made for Instagram Reels and TikTok. Set a clip to 9:16, or to 4:5 or 1:1 for the feed, crop it or fit it whole over a blurred copy, trim and split it on a timeline, change its speed, and add texts that show for a stretch of time. Captions are timed word by word, in five looks: make them free in your browser, or fast with a paid option that shows its price before you start. Add music, pick the cover, check the length against Reels, Stories and TikTok, then save an MP4 next to the original or download it. The editor opens from Tools, from Edit video in the library, from the full size viewer, from Edit on a video in History, and from the pencil on the clip of a TikTok or Instagram post. The Image editor gains a Social panel: pick X, Instagram or LinkedIn and a placement (a feed post, a story, a banner, a profile photo), crop the picture or fit it whole over a blurred or plain background, see what the network's buttons cover and how it will show, read the checks, and the Save panel is set to the file that network wants. hubStudio now sends its own Monday digest of what changed, with a Weekly digest switch in User Settings and an unsubscribe link in every mail. Also: a Play button under the TikTok preview, a post sent for validation now links its pictures to the Assets Library, and a PDF in the library no longer offers PDF Tools.

title: TikTok: a real TikTok preview, captions to TikTok's rules

blocks.text: The publishing step now shows your post the way TikTok does, the clip full screen with the caption over it, and the clip plays right there: tap to play, tap to pause, and drag along the bar to any moment. The caption box is clearer: a titled box, a field for your brief and the button under it. Captions written with AI follow TikTok's current rules, researched this month: the hook and the words people search for up front, 3 to 5 specific hashtags, an open question to close, no link, no asking for likes. A new AI-generated content choice labels a clip made with AI, ticked for you when hubStudio rendered it. Clips picked from the Assets Library now show their first frame.

title: Maker logos on the Explore cards

blocks.text: Every card on Explore now shows the logo of the company that makes the engine, such as OpenAI, Google, ByteDance or Kling, so you can tell the engines apart at a glance.

The Assets Library joins the menu: your uploads and everything the team makes, in folders. Its Tools hold the new Image editor and the Image anonymizer. The editor crops to the size of each social network, turns and mirrors, adjusts the light and colors, applies a look, adds text, arrows and boxes, and places a logo, then saves a copy next to the original, a new version of an upload, or a download. It opens from the Assets Library, the full size viewer, the Image studio, History and the picture of a post.

title: Sign in page in your language

blocks.text: The sign in page now greets you in the language of your browser and shows a language picker, so you can switch before signing in. The logo on that page is larger too.
After sign in the connection check result now appears as a small notification in the corner instead of a band across the page. Press Escape to close the notification.

The hubStudio help center is now published at hubstudio.ai/help with step by step articles covering Explore, the Image and Video studios, History, Skills, Team, Clients, the balance and payments, your account and more. The guides include real app screenshots to help you find features and settings quickly.

Social networks are split into separate guides for LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and X, each with the right formats, publishing options and limits so you can prepare posts correctly. Links from Getting started, Skills, Validation, Your team and Account now point to the appropriate network article.

title: Your social networks, one module each

blocks.text: LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and X now each have a module of their own in the menu. Write a post there, schedule it or publish it on the accounts you connect on My Connections, in the menu under your picture.

An admin adds the companies the team works for under Clients on the Team page and gives their people a login. A client login opens on its Client space and sees only the work made for its company: it downloads it, comments on it and approves it. Client logins hold no balance.

title: Made for: tag work with its client

blocks.text: Say which client a piece was made for: pick it under Made for in the image and video studios, on a card in History or on a post. That client's people then find it in their Client space.

Send an image, a video or a post for approval to a teammate or to one of the client's people. They get an email with the link, open the piece full size, comment on it, and approve it or send it back. Every version stays in the thread.

title: Four roles: Admin, Creator, Viewer, Client

blocks.text: Creators make the images, videos and posts from the team's balance. Viewers see the team's work and spend nothing. Clients see only what was made for their company.

title: A check of your accounts after sign-in

blocks.text: After you sign in, hubStudio checks your social accounts in the background. When one needs attention, a band over the page says which one and what to do; close it with the cross or the Escape key.

title: Explore stays current on its own

blocks.text: Engines that are added or retired appear in Explore, or leave it, without waiting for an update of hubStudio.
hubStudio emails now carry the hubStudio look: a navy band with the logo on top and orange buttons.
**Create images and videos with the best engines, from one prepaid balance.**

list: **Explore** every image and video engine in one gallery: who makes it, what it does (text to image, image editing, upscaling, text to video, image to video, video from references) and what one run costs. Search, filter by use or by maker, sort by price, and open any engine straight into its studio.
**Image studio**: render from a prompt, edit a picture you upload, or upscale and restore one. Every option each engine sells is in the form, with the price shown before you run.
**Video studio**: film a prompt, animate a still, or follow pictures and clips you attach, with the price per second shown before the render.
**History** keeps everything you and your team made, newest first: open it full size, download it, or send its prompt back to the studio for a variation.

**Skills** shape how "Improve with AI" rewrites your prompts: fourteen ready skills for images and video (packshots, lifestyle scenes, a consistent character, text inside an image, camera moves, vertical video ads and more), plus the social network formats. Add them to your own skills and make them yours.

**Work alone or as a team.** Sign up for yourself, create a team, or ask to join one. A team shares one balance; administrators invite people, answer requests to join and set a daily limit per member.
**A prepaid balance**, topped up by card, Alipay or WeChat Pay, with automatic top-up on a saved card and an invoice for every top-up.
